findings.title: G5 at a 150 ms round trip has no margin under the cap, so with 10% loss as well 'tick never returns false' fails for some seeds
findings.claim: G5 now requires `tick` never to return false. At 150 ms round trip the lead when a publication arrives is about 9 ticks, plus a tick of pump granularity. The first publication after a 300 ms outage of publications arrives up to one cadence (50 ms, 3 ticks) after the outage ends. So P reaches 9 + 18 + 3 = 30 ticks past the last confirmed tick, which is PREDICT_MAX_TICKS. §3.5's own figure ('At a 150 ms lead that is about 350 ms') is exactly 300 ms of outage plus one cadence. G5 also runs 10% publication loss in the same case. If the publication just before or just after the outage is lost, the gap grows by another 50 ms, past the cap, and `tick` returns false. The fix for R1-F11 turned the old, tautological 'never stops while within the cap' into this stronger check, and that is what produced the problem.
findings.evidence: spec L213 (G5: 50 and 150 ms, 10% loss plus a 300 ms outage, 'tick never returns false'); spec L121 (§3.5: 150 ms lead ⇒ about 350 ms before the cap); spec L109 (cap 30, false at the cap); spec L99 (measured target = T plus the local ticks since the anchor); src/network/state/sender.ts:L13 (STATE_CADENCE_TICKS = 3)
findings.why: Whether the gate passes depends on the seed and on pump timing. Implementers will either fish for a passing seed or weaken the check, which is the failure mode R1-F1 and R1-F2 were raised to stop.
findings.fix: Keep the cap and change the case. Either run the 300 ms outage only at 50 ms round trip, or use 150 ms with a 250 ms outage. In either case, apply no random loss to the publication before and the publication after the outage window. Alternatively, state the bound: past the cap, `tick` returns false for at most the gap's excess over (30 − lead) ticks.

findings.title: G1(a) cannot pass at 50 ms round trip or more: the first anchored publication after every reset must re-simulate
findings.claim: After a reset, the log is cleared and the offset maps the newest local tick to T, so the lead is 0 (§3.4 step 1, Reset). Frames sent after the reset are acknowledged only a round trip later. The first publication that holds an anchor then moves the measured target by the whole lead: about 3 ticks at 50 ms, 9 at 150 ms and 18 at 300 ms. That is more than the 2-tick allowance, so step 4 fails and step 5 re-simulates. G1(a) requires 'every cadence publication after the first' to verify, so it fails once per round start at every non-zero round trip in its matrix. At 5% loss, three held frames lost in a row also move the anchor by 3 and force a re-simulation, even though the inputs are constant.
findings.evidence: spec L97 (after a reset the offset maps the newest local tick to T; no lead until the first anchor); spec L99 (target from the anchor; 2-tick allowance); spec L100-L101 (outside the allowance ⇒ re-simulated); spec L111 (reset clears the log); spec L209 (G1(a): 'every cadence publication after the first verifies' at 50/150/300 ms)
findings.why: The gate cannot pass as written. That re-simulation is the designed way the lead is built, so it is not a bug the implementer can fix.
findings.fix: Reword G1(a) to 'every cadence publication after the first anchored one verifies, except one re-simulation per anchor shift of more than 2 ticks, and every re-simulation leaves P's state unchanged (equal hash before and after)'. Alternatively, require 'P's state at every confirmed tick hashes equal to the publication', which is the property G1 names, and report the verified/resimulated split.

findings.title: Step 1 drops commands that have not run yet when their entry is at or before the anchor
findings.claim: Step 1 drops every entry at or before the anchor's local tick, and removes only the commands with sequence <= c from the entries that remain. A command whose entry falls at or before the anchor but whose sequence is above c is still waiting at the authority, and it is dropped with its entry. This happens when the reliable command reaches the authority after a later held frame. Held frames go on 'unreliable-latest'. Commands go on 'reliable-ordered', and in receive-time mode they wait in a per-player outbox that flushes only when allowed and on ACK. P then lacks that command until C shows its result. The command shows on the next tick, vanishes, then comes back. That is a toggle flicker for something like laserMode, not the tick-or-two error the 'Step 2 is an estimate' paragraph describes.
findings.evidence: spec L97 ('Entries at or before the anchor's local tick are dropped. Commands with sequence <= c are removed from the entries that hold them'); spec L105 (the only stated effect of a command arriving apart from its frame is 'off by a tick or two'); src/renderer/src/clientControl/streamClient.ts:L208 (held on unreliable-latest), L209-L214 (commands to the outbox when receiveTime, flushed separately)
findings.why: This is visible on the Weapons and Helm consoles under loss, in ordinary online play. Two implementers could reasonably build it either way, and the spec's description of the error understates it.
findings.fix: In step 1, carry the remaining commands (sequence > c) from dropped entries onto the first entry after the anchor. If none exists, carry them onto tick T + 1. Keep the risk row's guarantee: a command leaves the log only by c. State this in the estimate paragraph.

findings.title: The log and the per-tick records are never trimmed while this seat is not producing
findings.claim: Step 1 drops entries only up to an anchor. Not-producing entries have a null sequence and never become anchors. While the window is unfocused, the log, the per-tick input records and the hashes therefore grow by 60 a second for as long as focus is away. Step 2 reads only the entries from local tick T + 1 − offset onward, so everything older is dead weight.
findings.evidence: spec L86 (not-producing entries: null sequence); spec L97 (no anchor ⇒ offset kept, nothing dropped); spec L89 (per-tick records)
findings.why: It is a slow leak on an alt-tabbed window, and an implementer has to invent the trim rule.
findings.fix: Add to step 1: whether or not an anchor is found, drop entries and records at local ticks at or before T − offset, and records at ticks before T.
